\(56^\circ + 34^\circ = 90^\circ\) means 56 and 34 are the measures of complimentary angles.
\(\sin \theta = \cos (90 - \theta)\)
\(\therefore\) \(\sin 34^\circ = \cos (90 - 34)^\circ = \cos 56^\circ\)
\(\therefore\) \(\dfrac{\cos 56^\circ}{\sin 34^\circ} = \dfrac{\cos 56^\circ}{\cos 56^\circ} = 1\)

stem: In right angled \(\Delta\) ACB, if \(\angle C = 90^\circ\), \(AC = 3\), \(BC = 4\). Find the ratios \(\sin A\), \(\sin B\), \(\cos A\), \(\tan B\).
solution:
In right angled \(\Delta\) ACB, using Pythagoras' theorem,
\(AB^{2} = AC^{2} + BC^{2}\)
\(= 3^{2} + 4^{2} = 5^{2}\)
\(\therefore\) \(AB = 5\)
\(\sin A = \dfrac{BC}{AB} = \dfrac{4}{5}\)  and  \(\cos A = \dfrac{AC}{AB} = \dfrac{3}{5}\)
\(\sin B = \dfrac{AC}{AB} = \dfrac{3}{5}\)  and  \(\tan B = \dfrac{AC}{BC} = \dfrac{3}{4}\)
_note: The book prints the four ratios in two columns (sin A and cos A on one line, sin B and tan B on the next); linearised here into two lines with the same pairing. The stem is fully self-contained — Fig. 8.22 merely redraws the triangle whose two legs the stem already states, so no figure is needed to answer.

stem: In right angled triangle \(\Delta\) PQR, \(\angle Q = 90^\circ\), \(\angle R = \theta\) and if \(\sin \theta = \dfrac{5}{13}\) then find \(\cos \theta\) and \(\tan \theta\).
solution:
In right angled \(\Delta\) PQR, \(\angle R = \theta\)
\(\sin \theta = \dfrac{5}{13}\)
\(\therefore\) \(\dfrac{PQ}{PR} = \dfrac{5}{13}\)
\(\therefore\) Let \(PQ = 5k\) and \(PR = 13k\)
Let us find QR by using Pythagoras' theorem,
\(PQ^{2} + QR^{2} = PR^{2}\)
\((5k)^{2} + QR^{2} = (13k)^{2}\)
\(25k^{2} + QR^{2} = 169k^{2}\)
\(QR^{2} = 169k^{2} - 25k^{2}\)
\(QR^{2} = 144k^{2}\)
\(QR = 12k\)
Now, in right angled \(\Delta\) PQR, \(PQ = 5k\), \(PR = 13k\) and \(QR = 12k\)
\(\therefore\) \(\cos \theta = \dfrac{QR}{PR} = \dfrac{12k}{13k} = \dfrac{12}{13}\),  \(\tan \theta = \dfrac{PQ}{QR} = \dfrac{5k}{12k} = \dfrac{5}{12}\)
_note: STITCHED ACROSS THE 119/120 PAGE BREAK. The stem and the first three lines of the solution (down to \(PQ/PR = 5/13\)) are at the foot of 0-based 119; 0-based 120 opens at "\(\therefore\) Let PQ = 5k and PR = 13k" and carries the Pythagoras working through to the final \(\cos \theta = 12/13\) and \(\tan \theta = 5/12\). Both halves are transcribed here. Figures 8.23 (119) and 8.24 (120) are the same triangle, unlabelled then labelled 5k/12k/13k; the stem is self-contained so neither is needed to answer.

stem: Which of the following statements is true ?
_note: Derived. In a right-angled triangle the two acute angles are complementary, and the side opposite one is the side adjacent to the other - so the sine of an angle equals the cosine of its complement. Hence (A) holds for every acute theta. (B) and (C) equate a bounded ratio (cos, sin, both at most 1) with tan, which is unbounded, so each fails at once: at theta = 30 degrees, cos 30 = 0.866 while tan 60 = 1.732, and sin 30 = 0.5 while tan 60 = 1.732. (D) would force tan theta = tan(90 - theta) for all theta, i.e. tan theta = cot theta, which holds only at theta = 45 degrees, not identically - at 30 degrees it reads 0.577 = 1.732, false.
